newsitem.title: USA: Gaylord Q4 cable cash flow, revenues rose.
newsitem.headline: Gaylord Q4 cable cash flow, revenues rose.

text.p: Gaylord Entertainment Co said Monday its cable networks' operating cash flow totaled $23.4 million in the fourth quarter, an increase of 33.9 percent from the year earlier quarter, on a 20.1 percent increase in revenues to $84.3 million.
Earlier, Westinghouse Electric Corp announced plans to acquire Gaylord's cable units in exchange for stock with a value of $1.55 billion.
Gaylord said the cable networks division's results for the quarter reflect increased costs related to Country Music Television International.

It said this was primarily due to the acquisition of a 24-hour transponder in Europe in September 1996. Total operating losses related to CMT International for the fourth quarter of 1996 rose to $5.7 million from $3.2 million for the same quarter in 1995.

The company earned $0.28 per share in the fourth quarter, an increase of 21.7 percent, while operating cash flow (operating income plus depreciation and amortization) increased 12.6 percent to $55.1 million.
Total revenues in the latest quarter of 1996 were $194.0 million, an increase of 11.1 percent over a year earlier.

The company sold KHTV, a television station in Houston, in January 1996. On a comparable basis, which excludes the 1995 operating results of KHTV, total revenues rose 16.8 percent in the latest quarter.
For the full year of 1996, revenues increased 5.6 percent to $747.2 million. Excluding revenues generated in 1995 by

KHTV, total revenues increased 10.9 percent during 1996. Operating cash flow for 1996 rose 19.1 percent to $178.5 million from $149.9 million. Excluding a $13.3 million noncash writedown of television program inventories from the 1995 results, operating cash flow increased 9.4 percent.
In 1996, the company said, it recorded a nonrecurring gain on the sale of KHTV of $73.9 million ($43.5 million net of tax, or $0.44 per share).

The company said it had several nonrecurring gains and losses during 1995 including the television program inventory writedown ($8.2 million net of taxes, or $0.08 per share), a loss upon the disposal of the company's interest in the Fiesta Texas theme park of $5.5 million ($3.4 million net of taxes, or $0.04 per share), and a gain on the sale of its cable television systems segment of $73.8 million ($43.0 million net of taxes, or $0.44 per share).

Excluding these nonrecurring gains and losses from reported results, net income was $87.7 million, or $0.90 per share in 1996, a 13.9 percnet increase over the comparable 1995 results of $77.0 million, or $0.79 per share.
